notes:
I wasn't able to do this research, so I haven't written any verse notes.

I tried to load six commentary pages at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, and Wesley's notes on studylight.org. They didn't load cleanly, a bug in my script stopped me from seeing what came back, and the tool then stopped me from running any more lookups in this conversation turn. I never read a single page. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have nothing sourced, I've left the notes out rather than give you unsourced commentary.

If you reply (even just "continue"), I'll start again in a new turn. I'd work through:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Wesley on biblehub.com and studylight.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own teachers on the sites you listed. The likely points are the four titles in v. 6, especially "Everlasting Father" and "Mighty God"; when and how v. 1 is fulfilled in Galilee (Matthew 4); and how literally to take the endless reign in v. 7.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey on modern scholarship. One example is the view that v. 6 refers to a royal birth or enthronement, perhaps Hezekiah. Then New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, plus any popular modern teaching I can actually find on those sites.

I'll fetch fewer pages at a time so one failure doesn't lose the whole batch. Every point will come with its page URL.
